definition.description: From a tall stationary bilateral stance on a clear, level, non-slip surface, make repeated low-amplitude vertical hops with simultaneous two-foot takeoff and landing. Contacts remain quiet, centred, and spring-like; the ankles and feet provide the visible primary motion while the knees and hips remain softly available rather than locked. One hop is one takeoff and one bilateral landing. This excludes travel, unilateral or alternating contacts, a rope, obstacle clearance, high-amplitude jumping, a squat-jump strategy, a sprint drill, and an assessment.

faultCorrections.loss_of_balance: end the set, restore a safe stationary base, or choose another reviewed task after revalidation
faultCorrections.cadence_decay: take more recovery or end the repeated-contact work rather than chasing fatigue
